source_review.notes: Checked twelve primary sources: the original Google MapReduce publication; current Apache Hadoop MapReduce, Apache Spark RDD/configuration/tuning/YARN/monitoring, Apache Flink network-buffer/blocking-shuffle/metrics, and Dask shuffle documentation. All twelve URLs returned HTTP 200 on the retrieval date. Sources support partitioned exchange, producer and reducer lifecycles, indexed consolidation, push and external shuffle services, network buffers, blocking shuffle, monitoring, and distributed shuffle trade-offs.

evidence: Reviewed accepted producers M, destinations R, exchange E, block B_{i,j}, consumer multiset C_j, destination bytes D_j, total D, mean D-bar, skew K, remote bytes, and throughput Q.
Checked logical blocks, physical files/chunks, producer attempts, exchange generations, indexes, locations, candidates, winners, pushes, fetches, and commits remain distinct.
Verified logical, serialized, compressed, spilled, local, remote, retried, replicated, and discarded byte measures are not conflated.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Set, multiset, byte, count, and time quantities are defined with explicit scope; engine-specific counters are qualified.

evidence: Executed shuffle-matrix-accounting with Python 3.14.4 and reproduced 8 producers, 4 consumers, 32 logical blocks, and 16 indexed physical files.
Recomputed destination total 1,016 MiB, mean 254 MiB, maximum destination 460 MiB, and skew ratio 1.81.
Recomputed Exercise 1 as 960,000 logical cells and 2,400 physical indexed files, and Exercise 3 as 80 GiB total, 16 GiB mean, 2.75 skew, and a 48-second bandwidth floor.
numerical_recomputation.notes: The runnable fixture validates deterministic accounting only, not an engine, transfer, storage, or failure simulation.

evidence: Verified N_b=MR and B_{i,j} contains exactly producer-i records mapped to destination j by pinned p_E.
Checked disjoint per-producer destination sets union to I_i when the routing function is total and single-valued.
Checked C_j is the multiset union of exactly one accepted contribution per producer and K=max_j D_j/(D/R) for D>0.
Reviewed D_remote/Q as a conditional throughput lower bound rather than a latency prediction.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: Routing correctness relies on stable compatible routing and accepted-attempt authority; physical realization does not change the logical proof.

evidence: Reviewed empty blocks, zero payload, many tiny blocks, one huge block, exact buffer limits, high M and R, hot keys, compute-only skew, incompressible input, and partial push coverage.
Reviewed producer death before/after publication, executor/node/service loss, stale locations, speculative losers, mixed generations, consumer retry, and coordinator recovery.
Reviewed corrupt/truncated index or data, checksum mismatch, format incompatibility, authentication/throttling, slow progress, retry amplification, and cleanup races.
Reviewed all buffers occupied by incomplete work, control-plane starvation, hidden off-heap/cache memory, connection/file-descriptor exhaustion, and decompression attacks.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Correctness, availability, bounded resources, durability, and performance can fail independently and have separate evidence.

evidence: Traced run/exchange, plan, partitioner, format, producer partition, attempt, destination, index, block, location, consumer, and committed-output identities.
Checked only accepted attempts publish complete validated blocks and consumers cannot omit, duplicate, or mix contributions.
Checked index/data binding, ranges, length, checksum, codec, serializer, encryption, and generation compatibility.
Checked finite buffer/request/connection/disk budgets, reserved progress capacity, invalidation, failure recovery, and reference-aware cleanup.
invariant_checking.notes: The exchange directory is authoritative for accepted generations; storage listings and task-success messages alone are insufficient.

evidence: Reviewed the ten-step audit from exchange contract and logical matrix through publication, directory, transport, flow control, consumption, attempt correctness, measurement, fault injection, and governance.
Checked the routing proof requires a total single-valued pinned partition function and exactly one accepted attempt per producer.
Checked the conditional resource-safety argument requires complete charging, finite budgets, release on terminal paths, reserved control capacity, and no credit-holding wait cycle.

Reviewed counterexamples for shuffle-equals-network, MR-files, task-success publication, arbitrary speculative success, unlimited concurrency, mean-based tails, remote-service infallibility, listing authority, and unconditional cleanup.
proof_review.notes: Logical correctness, physical durability, and progress are proved under explicit assumptions rather than inferred from successful final output.

evidence: Audited uses of exactly, complete, accepted, visible, authoritative, deterministic, durable, safe, bounded, minimum, lower bound, and deadlock.
Confirmed D_remote/Q is labeled coarse and omits overlap, topology, disk, CPU, requests, congestion, and tails.
Confirmed remote, external, push, pipelined, checksummed, and replicated designs are not labeled universally faster or reliable.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: Engine-specific behavior is sourced and architecture choices remain conditional on workload, deployment, and recovery contracts.

evidence: Reviewed proposed producer, directory, consumer, push, fetch, flow-control, retry, skew, cleanup, and telemetry-loss measurements.
Confirmed no universal buffer size, partition count, request limit, timeout, codec, replication factor, remote-service architecture, skew threshold, or retention period is prescribed.
Checked that average, quantile, maximum, logical/physical, local/remote, useful/retried, and byte/record/CPU distributions remain separated.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: Production tuning requires representative payload, key, compression, topology, disk/network, concurrency, failure, cost, and policy evidence.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed shuffle as a partitioned exchange protocol spanning logical routing, physical layout, producer publication, directory metadata, pull/push transport, blocking/pipelined semantics, storage ownership, flow control, recovery, skew, observability, validation, and governance.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed practical designs for indexed files, attempt-scoped candidates, authoritative winner metadata, request/byte budgets, consumer streaming, location refresh, classification and retry, remote service operation, skew diagnosis, fault injection, and reference-aware deletion. Internal practitioner-oriented review only.

pedagogical_review.notes: Verified progression from logical matrix and physical layout through producer, directory, transport, consumer, failure, accounting, and lifecycle. Ten examples and five fully answered exercises cover scale, publication, speculation, flow control, byte semantics, elasticity, skew, corruption, push, and governance.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external Spark, Flink, Hadoop, or Dask maintainer, shuffle-service operator, distributed-systems researcher, storage/network/performance specialist, security/privacy/legal/records authority, affected-tenant reviewer, accessibility specialist, or certification review is claimed.
